# MagicInput

> MagicInput shares one keyboard and mouse between a Mac (macOS 13+) and a Windows PC (10/11) on the same local network. Push the pointer off the edge of one screen and it continues on the other, with keyboard and copied text following. Encrypted, paired with a short code, no account or cloud.

To install it for someone, follow the runbook: it covers detecting the OS, installing, telling the first computer from the second with `magicinput status --json`, pairing, verifying and troubleshooting.

## Docs

- [AI setup runbook](https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/blob/main/docs/AI_SETUP.md): step-by-step install and pairing for AI assistants
- [README](https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/blob/main/README.md): features, install, quick start, controls, tips
- [Architecture](https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): processes, protocol, security model
- [Security](https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/blob/main/SECURITY.md): security boundaries and reporting
- [Pricing and licensing](https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/blob/main/PRICING.md): free for personal use with every feature; business use needs a license ($10/month, $96/year or $199 once, all computers)

## Downloads

- macOS (notarized, universal): https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/releases/latest/download/MagicInput.dmg, or `brew install --cask betoxf/tap/magicinput`
- Windows: https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput/releases/latest/download/MagicInput-Setup.exe (`/S` for a silent install)
- Build from source: https://github.com/betoxf/Magicinput#build-from-source
